description: Comprehensive question bank derived from Indian_Geography.pdf (Sections 3.5.1–3.5.22). All questions are unique, exam-oriented, and structured for KEA examination use.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: India lies in which hemispheres?
questions.explanation: India lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres, in South Asia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the approximate latitudinal extents of India's mainland?
questions.explanation: The mainland extends approximately from 8°4'N to 37°6'N latitude.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the approximate longitudinal extents of India's mainland?
questions.explanation: The mainland extends approximately from 68°7'E to 97°25'E longitude.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Including islands, what is the latitude of India's southernmost point, Indira Point?
questions.explanation: Indira Point on Great Nicobar is at about 6°45'N.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The longitudinal span of India produces a local-time difference of roughly how many hours between the eastern and western extremities?
questions.explanation: The longitudinal span produces a local-time difference of roughly two hours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is India's total geographical area?
questions.explanation: India covers approximately 3.287 million km² (3,287,263 km²).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is India's rank in the world by geographical area?
questions.explanation: India is the seventh-largest country in the world by area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What percentage of the world's land area does India account for?
questions.explanation: India accounts for about 2.4% of the world's land area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.explanation: 82°30'E longitude is India's Standard Meridian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Standard Meridian of India passes near which town in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: 82°30'E passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Indian Standard Time (IST) is set at which UTC offset?
questions.explanation: IST is UTC + 5 hours 30 minutes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does India use a single standard time despite its large east-west extent?

options.A: To avoid confusion in international trade only
options.B: To facilitate administration, transport, broadcasting, commerce and coordination
options.C: Because local solar time does not vary across India
options.D: Because the Constitution mandates a single time zone

questions.explanation: A single standard time facilitates administration, transport, broadcasting, commerce and coordination.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer is located at which latitude?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is at 23°30'N.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: It crosses eight states from Gujarat to Mizoram.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.explanation: The eight states are Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha is not among them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is India's southernmost point including islands?
questions.explanation: Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island is India's southernmost point including islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which countries share land borders with India?

options.A: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan
options.B: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka
options.C: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Maldives
options.D: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Thailand

questions.explanation: India shares land borders with Pakistan, Afghanistan (in India's official territorial claim), China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are India's maritime neighbours?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka and the Maldives are maritime neighbours of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pakistan is located to which direction of India?
questions.explanation: Pakistan is to the west/northwest of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Bangladesh is located to which direction of India?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh is to the east of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a land boundary and a maritime boundary?

options.A: A land boundary separates national territories on land; a maritime boundary delimits sea areas and associated rights between states
options.B: A land boundary is always disputed; a maritime boundary is always settled
options.C: A land boundary is defined by UNCLOS; a maritime boundary is defined by the Survey of India

questions.explanation: A land boundary separates national territories on land, while a maritime boundary delimits sea areas and associated rights between states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Under UNCLOS, up to how many nautical miles can a coastal state claim a territorial sea from its baseline?
questions.explanation: A coastal state may claim a territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles from its baseline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Under UNCLOS, up to how many nautical miles may an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extend?
questions.explanation: An EEZ may extend up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In the Exclusive Economic Zone, what rights does the coastal state have?

options.B: Sovereign rights over natural resources but not full national territory

questions.explanation: In the EEZ, the coastal state has sovereign rights over natural resources, but it is not full national territory.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the continental shelf under UNCLOS?

options.A: The submerged natural prolongation of the land territory
options.B: The territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles
options.C: The high seas beyond the EEZ
options.D: The internal waters landward of the baseline

questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the submerged natural prolongation of the land territory, as defined under UNCLOS.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the significance of the continental shelf for a coastal state?

options.A: The state has sovereign rights over seabed and subsoil resources
options.B: The state has no rights over the shelf
options.C: The shelf is part of the high seas
options.D: The shelf is limited to 12 nautical miles

questions.explanation: Coastal states have sovereign rights over seabed and subsoil resources on the continental shelf.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the revised coastline length of India promulgated in April 2025?
questions.explanation: The revised Survey of India/National Hydrographic Office figure is 11,098.81 km, promulgated in April 2025.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does the revised coastline figure of 11,098.81 km differ from the older figure of 7,516.6 km?

options.A: A physical sudden change in India's coastline occurred
options.B: It reflects measurement scale and method, including mainland and island coastlines
options.D: The revised figure includes maritime boundaries

questions.explanation: The revised figure reflects measurement scale and method, not a physical sudden change.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Radcliffe Line divided British India into which two countries in 1947?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line divided British India into India and Pakistan in 1947 and was also used in the partition of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Line of Control (LoC) is the military control line between India and which country?
questions.explanation: The LoC is the military control line in Jammu and Kashmir between India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Line of Actual Control (LAC) refers to the contested boundary alignment between India and which country?
questions.explanation: The LAC refers to the contested boundary alignment between India and China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The McMahon Line is associated with which sector of the India-China boundary?
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line is the boundary line proposed in the 1914 Simla Convention for the eastern sector.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Durand Line?
questions.explanation: The Durand Line is the Afghanistan-Pakistan boundary, not an India border.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important Himalayan pass?
questions.explanation: Zoji La is an important Himalayan pass. Khyber and Bolan are in Pakistan; Salang is in Afghanistan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the six major physiographic divisions of India?

options.A: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands
options.B: Himalayas, Deccan Plateau, Thar Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands, Ghats
options.C: Himalayas, Indo-Gangetic Plain, Central Highlands, Thar Desert, Eastern Ghats, Andaman Islands
options.D: Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands, Rann of Kachchh

questions.explanation: The six divisions are Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physiographic division is described as 'young fold mountains with high peaks, glaciers and deep valleys'?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are young fold mountains with high peaks, glaciers, deep valleys and major river sources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physiographic division is formed by vast alluvial lowlands deposited by the Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra river systems?
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains are vast alluvial lowlands formed by the Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra river systems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physiographic division is an ancient stable shield of igneous and metamorphic rocks, rich in minerals?
questions.explanation: The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient stable shield of igneous and metamorphic rocks, mineral-rich uplands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indian Desert is also known as which region?
questions.explanation: The Indian Desert is the arid Thar region with sparse rainfall, dunes and ephemeral streams.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physiographic division includes the Andaman-Nicobar volcanic/tectonic island arc and Lakshadweep coral islands?
questions.explanation: The Islands division includes the Andaman-Nicobar volcanic/tectonic island arc and Lakshadweep coral islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How were the Himalayas formed?

options.A: By volcanic eruptions in the Indian Ocean
options.B: By convergence and collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate after closure of the Tethys Ocean

questions.explanation: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by convergence and collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate after closure of the Tethys Ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happened to the sediments deposited in the former ocean basin during the formation of the Himalayas?

options.A: They were compressed, folded, faulted and uplifted
options.B: They were subducted into the mantle

questions.explanation: The sediments were compressed, folded, faulted and uplifted, making the region tectonically active.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the major longitudinal divisions of the Himalayas from north to south?

options.A: Shiwalik, Lesser Himalaya, Greater Himalaya, Trans-Himalaya
options.B: Trans-Himalaya, Greater Himalaya, Lesser Himalaya, Shiwalik
options.C: Greater Himalaya, Trans-Himalaya, Shiwalik, Lesser Himalaya
options.D: Lesser Himalaya, Greater Himalaya, Trans-Himalaya, Shiwalik

questions.explanation: From north to south, the belts are Trans-Himalaya, Greater Himalaya (Himadri), Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and Shiwalik.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range includes the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zanskar ranges?
questions.explanation: The Trans-Himalaya lies north of the Great Himalaya and includes the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zanskar ranges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range is the highest and most continuous, with snow-covered peaks and major glaciers?
questions.explanation: The Greater Himalaya (Himadri) is the highest and most continuous range, with average heights commonly above 6,000 m.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range is the outermost and youngest, composed of unconsolidated sediments?
questions.explanation: The Shiwalik is the outermost and youngest foothill range, with unconsolidated sediments and longitudinal valleys called duns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range includes the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, with valleys and hill stations?
questions.explanation: The Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) includes the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, valleys and hill stations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers form major deltas along the Eastern Coastal Plain of India?
questions.explanation: The Eastern Coastal Plain contains large deltas formed by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a lagoon located along the Eastern Coastal Plain of India?
questions.explanation: Chilika is a lagoon on the Eastern Coastal Plain. The PDF also identifies Pulicat as an important eastern coastal lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pulicat Lake is identified in the PDF as which type of coastal feature?
questions.explanation: Pulicat is one of the important lagoons situated along India's Eastern Coastal Plain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a delta?

options.A: A deep valley formed by glacial erosion
options.B: A landform formed by the accumulation of river sediments at the river mouth
options.C: A coastal cliff formed by wave erosion
options.D: A mountain formed by volcanic activity

questions.explanation: A delta develops when a river deposits sediments at its mouth. Such deposits may be associated with the formation of distributary channels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is commonly associated with the formation of a river delta?
questions.explanation: River sediment accumulation at the river mouth may lead to the formation of distributaries, which are channels branching away from the main river.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an estuary?

options.A: A freshwater lake surrounded by mountains
options.B: A tidal river mouth where freshwater mixes with seawater
options.C: A river channel that originates from a glacier
options.D: A freshwater wetland found only in deserts

questions.explanation: An estuary is a tidal river mouth where freshwater mixes with seawater. Sediments may be flushed seaward by tidal and river processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the general difference between the eastern and western coastal river mouths of India?

options.A: Eastern rivers commonly form deltas, while many west-flowing rivers form estuaries
options.B: Eastern rivers commonly form estuaries, while western rivers form large deltas
options.C: Both coasts have only inland drainage

questions.explanation: The PDF explains that east-flowing rivers commonly form deltas, whereas many west-flowing rivers enter the sea through estuaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic coastal feature of the Western Coastal Plain?

options.A: Large river deltas along its entire length
options.B: Estuaries, creeks, lagoons, and natural harbours
options.D: Inland salt lakes throughout the coast

questions.explanation: The Western Coastal Plain is associated with estuaries, creeks, lagoons, and natural harbours, particularly along the Konkan and Malabar coasts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which coastal region of India is particularly known for its backwater lagoon and canal system?
questions.explanation: The Malabar Coast of Kerala is known for its backwater system consisting of lagoons and canals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations consists entirely of ports listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Mumbai, Kochi, Chennai, and Visakhapatnam are among the major ports listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Deendayal Port, formerly known as Kandla Port, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Deendayal Port, formerly known as Kandla, among India's major ports. It is located in Gujarat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jawaharlal Nehru Port is included in the list of major ports of which country?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru Port is listed in the PDF among India's major ports.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is also known as Ennore Port?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Kamarajar Port by its earlier or commonly used name, Ennore Port.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: V.O. Chidambaranar Port is associated with which place?
questions.explanation: V.O. Chidambaranar Port, also identified with Tuticorin, is listed among the major ports of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a natural or sheltered harbour on the Indian coast?
questions.explanation: Kochi is among the natural or sheltered harbours mentioned in the PDF, along with Mumbai, Marmagao, and Visakhapatnam.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major ecological function of coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, coral reefs, and seagrass beds?
questions.explanation: Coastal ecosystems, including mangroves, coral reefs, seagrass beds, estuaries, and salt marshes, support fisheries and biodiversity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified in the PDF as a threat to India's coastal ecosystems?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists unplanned tourism among coastal ecosystem threats, along with coastal erosion, cyclones, sea-level rise, ports, sand mining, pollution, and wetland reclamation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in which water body?
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Lakshadweep Islands are located in which sea?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is an island group located in the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are mainly associated with which type of geological formation?
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are mainly associated with tectonic and volcanic island-arc formations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Lakshadweep Islands are mainly composed of which type of island formations?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep consists mainly of low-lying coral atolls and reefs, with sand cays formed through coral-related processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which island is identified as India's only confirmed active volcano?
questions.explanation: Barren Island, located in the Andaman Sea, is identified in the PDF as India's only confirmed active volcano.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about Narcondam Island is consistent with the PDF?

options.A: It is generally classified as dormant or inactive
options.B: It is India's only confirmed active volcano
options.C: It is a coral atoll in Lakshadweep
options.D: It is located in the Gulf of Mannar

questions.explanation: The PDF describes Narcondam as volcanic but generally classified as dormant or inactive in standard references.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which channel separates the Andaman group of islands from the Nicobar group?
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel, located approximately along 10°N latitude, separates the Andaman group from the Nicobar group.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Nine Degree Channel separates which island from the main Lakshadweep group?
questions.explanation: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy Island from the main Lakshadweep group.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which channel separates Minicoy Island from the Maldives?
questions.explanation: The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy Island from the Maldives.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Duncan Passage is located between which two islands?
questions.explanation: Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Palk Strait separates southeastern India from which country?
questions.explanation: Palk Strait separates southeastern India from the northern part of Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Gulf of Mannar is situated between which two regions?

options.A: Southern Tamil Nadu and western Sri Lanka

questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar lies south of Tamil Nadu and west of Sri Lanka. It contains coral reef and seagrass habitats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which point is identified as the southernmost point of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Point, situated on Great Nicobar Island, is identified in the PDF as India's southernmost point.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Indira Point was severely affected by which natural disaster in 2004?
questions.explanation: The PDF states that Indira Point was severely affected by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami and subsequent subsidence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an ecological concern affecting India's islands?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists freshwater scarcity among island-related ecological concerns, along with coral bleaching, sea-level rise, coastal erosion, invasive species, habitat fragmentation, tourism pressure, and cyclone or tsunami vulnerability.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major difference between Himalayan and Peninsular river systems?

options.A: Himalayan rivers are generally perennial, while Peninsular rivers are mostly rain-fed
options.B: Peninsular rivers are generally snow-fed, while Himalayan rivers are entirely rain-fed

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers are generally perennial because they receive water from snow and rainfall. Peninsular rivers are older and mostly rain-fed, with greater seasonal variation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists of the three major Himalayan river systems?
questions.explanation: The three major Himalayan river systems identified in the PDF are the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indus River rises near which lake in the Tibetan region?
questions.explanation: The Indus River rises near Lake Manasarovar in the Tibetan region before flowing through Ladakh and Pakistan towards the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Indus River?
questions.explanation: The Beas is one of the tributaries of the Indus system. Other tributaries listed in the PDF are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, and Sutlej.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which treaty governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus river system between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960. The PDF states that the eastern rivers—Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej—are allocated primarily to India, while the western rivers—Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab—are allocated primarily to Pakistan, subject to treaty provisions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which glacier is the source of the Bhagirathi River?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi River rises from the Gangotri Glacier at Gaumukh in Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which place do the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet to form the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag in Uttarakhand, where the river is known as the Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: By which name does the Ganga enter Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: After flowing through India, the Ganga enters Bangladesh as the Padma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Gomti is one of the tributaries of the Ganga. Other tributaries listed in the PDF include Yamuna, Ramganga, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Son, and Damodar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of tributaries of the Ganga mentioned in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, and Gandak are listed as tributaries of the Ganga. The other groups contain tributaries of Peninsular rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is listed as a tributary of the Ganga and is associated with the Bihar region?
questions.explanation: The Kosi is one of the tributaries of the Ganga listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers is also included among the tributaries of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Damodar is included in the list of Ganga tributaries provided in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Yamuna River originates from which glacier?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna River rises from the Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which place does the Yamuna join the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna flows south and southeast before joining the Ganga at Prayagraj.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Yamuna?
questions.explanation: The Chambal is a tributary of the Yamuna. Other tributaries listed in the PDF are Tons, Sind, Betwa, and Ken.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only tributaries of the Yamuna according to the PDF?
questions.explanation: Tons, Chambal, Sind, and Betwa are listed as tributaries of the Yamuna. Ken is another tributary mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which geographical region does the Brahmaputra River originate?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra rises on the Tibetan Plateau, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: By which name does the Brahmaputra River enter Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The river enters Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang or Dihang after flowing across the Tibetan Plateau as the Yarlung Tsangpo.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: After entering Bangladesh, the Brahmaputra is known as which river?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra enters Bangladesh as the Jamuna and joins the Padma–Meghna river system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is associated with the Brahmaputra River in Assam?

options.A: Braided channels and high sediment loads
options.D: Formation of a desert drainage basin

questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra in Assam is associated with braided channels, high sediment loads, and floods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists of major east-flowing Peninsular rivers?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, and Pennar among the major east-flowing Peninsular rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Into which water body do the major east-flowing Peninsular rivers generally drain?
questions.explanation: Major east-flowing Peninsular rivers such as the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri drain into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada is a major west-flowing Peninsular river that drains into the Arabian Sea through an estuary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair consists of major west-flowing Peninsular rivers?
questions.explanation: Narmada and Tapi are the two major west-flowing Peninsular rivers highlighted in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Through which type of valley do the Narmada and Tapi rivers flow?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Narmada and Tapi as west-flowing rivers associated with rift valleys.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes many short west-coast rivers of Peninsular India?

options.A: They are generally steep and monsoon-dependent
options.B: They are all perennial and snow-fed
options.C: They flow entirely through desert regions
options.D: They all form extensive inland lakes

questions.explanation: The PDF states that many short west-coast rivers are steep and depend heavily on monsoon rainfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where does the Godavari River originate?
questions.explanation: The Godavari originates at Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Godavari?
questions.explanation: Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari. Other tributaries listed in the PDF include Pranhita, Manjira, Purna, and Sabari.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Pranhita tributary of the Godavari is formed by the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Pranhita as a tributary of the Godavari formed by the Wardha and Wainganga rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Krishna River originates near which place?
questions.explanation: The Krishna River originates near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Krishna River?
questions.explanation: Bhima is a tributary of the Krishna. Other tributaries listed in the PDF include Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Koyna, and Musi.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mahanadi River originates from which region?
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi originates in the Sihawa Hills of Chhattisgarh and flows towards the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Mahanadi?
questions.explanation: Hasdeo is listed as a tributary of the Mahanadi. Other tributaries mentioned in the PDF are Seonath, Mand, Ib, and Tel.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where does the Kaveri River originate?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri River originates at Talakaveri in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Kaveri?
questions.explanation: Hemavati is a tributary of the Kaveri. Other tributaries listed in the PDF include Kabini, Shimsha, Bhavani, Amaravati, and Noyyal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Narmada River originates from which place?
questions.explanation: The Narmada originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westwards towards the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Narmada?
questions.explanation: Tawa is listed as a tributary of the Narmada. Other tributaries mentioned in the PDF are Hiran and Orsang.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Tapi River originates near which place in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Tapi, also known as Tapti, originates in the Satpura region near Multai in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following rivers is a tributary of the Tapi?
questions.explanation: Girna is a tributary of the Tapi. The PDF also lists Purna, Panjhra, and Waghur as Tapi tributaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Sabarmati River originates in which geographical region?
questions.explanation: The Sabarmati originates in the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Sabarmati?
questions.explanation: Hathmati is listed as a tributary of the Sabarmati. Other tributaries in the PDF include Wakal, Sei, Harnav, and Watrak.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mahi River drains into which water body?
questions.explanation: The Mahi River originates in the Vindhya region of Madhya Pradesh and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Mahi River?
questions.explanation: Som is listed as a tributary of the Mahi. Other tributaries mentioned in the PDF are Anas and Panam.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is meant by inland drainage?

options.A: A river system in which streams do not reach the sea and terminate in inland areas
options.B: A river system that flows only through coastal plains
options.C: A drainage system formed exclusively by glaciers
options.D: A river system that always drains into the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: Inland drainage refers to drainage in which streams do not reach the sea. They may terminate in inland lakes, salt flats, desert depressions, or disappear through evaporation or infiltration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region of India is identified in the PDF as an area of inland drainage?
questions.explanation: Western Rajasthan contains inland drainage systems, including the Luni system and ephemeral desert streams.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At Rudraprayag, which two rivers meet?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Rudraprayag as the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two rivers meet at Karnaprayag?
questions.explanation: Karnaprayag is identified in the PDF as the confluence of the Alaknanda and Pindar rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two rivers meet at Koodli in Karnataka to form the Tungabhadra?
questions.explanation: The Tunga and Bhadra rivers meet at Koodli in Karnataka to form the Tungabhadra River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Majuli, a major river island in India, is located in which river?
questions.explanation: Majuli is a major river island situated in the Brahmaputra River in Assam.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Majuli is historically recognised for being one of the world's largest what?
questions.explanation: The PDF describes Majuli as historically recognised as one of the world's largest inhabited river islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which processes are primarily responsible for changes in the boundaries and channels of river islands?
questions.explanation: River islands and channel boundaries can change over time due to erosion and deposition of sediments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Cauvery river-water dispute primarily involves which group of states and Union Territories?

options.A: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Cauvery dispute as involving Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river-water dispute involves Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Krishna river-water dispute involves Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ravi–Beas river-water dispute is associated with which group of states?

options.A: Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan, among others

questions.explanation: The PDF lists the Ravi–Beas dispute as involving Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and other concerned parties.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mahadayi river-water dispute is also associated with which river name?
questions.explanation: The PDF refers to the Mahadayi/Mandovi dispute, involving Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Mahanadi river-water dispute mentioned in the PDF is between which states?
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi river-water dispute is identified as involving Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Vansadhara river-water dispute involves which two states?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Vansadhara dispute as involving Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following factors can affect the status and settlement of inter-state river-water disputes?

options.A: Tribunal awards, court orders, and inter-state arrangements

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that tribunal awards, court orders, and other arrangements may change the status of inter-state river-water disputes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the basic objective of river interlinking?

options.A: To transfer water from selected river basins to other basins
options.B: To stop the flow of all rivers
options.C: To convert all rivers into inland lakes
options.D: To divert all rivers towards the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: River interlinking involves transferring water from selected river basins to other basins through infrastructure such as reservoirs, canals, and pumping systems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The National Perspective Plan for river interlinking has which two major components?
questions.explanation: The National Perspective Plan for river interlinking is divided into Himalayan and Peninsular components.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a potential benefit of river interlinking?

options.B: Increasing soil salinity in every region
options.C: Eliminating the need for water management

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies irrigation and drought mitigation as potential benefits of river interlinking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a concern associated with river interlinking?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies displacement, ecological-flow concerns, project costs, inter-state consent, sediment-related issues, and climate uncertainty as concerns associated with river interlinking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination contains only concerns associated with river interlinking as described in the PDF?

options.A: Ecological flows, displacement, cost, and inter-state consent
options.B: Tourism, coral bleaching, and coastal erosion
options.C: Glacier formation, volcanic activity, and desert winds
options.D: Port development, marine fisheries, and ocean currents

questions.explanation: The PDF lists ecological flows, displacement, costs, inter-state consent, sediment, and climate uncertainty as important concerns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Bhakra–Nangal Project is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra–Nangal Project is associated with the Sutlej River and serves irrigation, hydropower, and flood-moderation purposes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Damodar Valley Project is associated with which river system?
questions.explanation: The Damodar Valley Project is based on the Damodar River and its tributaries and is a multipurpose basin-development project.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hirakud Dam is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi River in Odisha. Its purposes include flood control, irrigation, and hydropower generation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Nagarjuna Sagar Project is associated with which river?
questions.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar is a major project on the Krishna River, associated with irrigation and hydropower.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Sardar Sarovar Project is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Project is associated with the Narmada River in Gujarat and supports irrigation, drinking-water supply, and hydropower.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Tehri Dam is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: Tehri Dam is constructed on the Bhagirathi River in Uttarakhand. Its purposes include hydropower, water supply, and flow regulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Tungabhadra Project is associated with which river?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra Project is constructed on the Tungabhadra River and serves irrigation and hydropower purposes in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Krishna Raja Sagara Dam is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Krishna Raja Sagara, commonly known as KRS, is a project on the Kaveri River in Karnataka, used for irrigation and water supply.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mettur Dam, also known as Stanley Reservoir, is constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: Mettur Dam, also known as Stanley Reservoir, is located on the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu and supports irrigation and water supply.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Rihand Dam is also associated with which reservoir name?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Rihand/Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar as a project on the Rihand River in Uttar Pradesh, associated with power and water supply.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Farakka Barrage is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Farakka Barrage is built across the Ganga in West Bengal. It regulates flows towards the Hooghly and supports navigation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following project–river pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Hirakud is associated with the Mahanadi River. Tehri is on the Bhagirathi, Bhakra–Nangal is on the Sutlej, and Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following project–state combinations is correctly matched according to the PDF?
questions.explanation: Hirakud is located in Odisha. The PDF lists Tehri in Uttarakhand, Mettur in Tamil Nadu, and Sardar Sarovar in Gujarat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which project is specifically associated with multipurpose basin development of the Damodar River and its tributaries?
questions.explanation: The Damodar Valley Project is identified as a multipurpose basin-development project associated with the Damodar River and its tributaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a stated purpose of the Bhakra–Nangal Project?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists irrigation, hydropower, and flood moderation as purposes of the Bhakra–Nangal Project.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indira Gandhi Canal carries water from which river system?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Canal carries water from the Sutlej–Beas system into Rajasthan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical region of Rajasthan has been significantly affected by irrigation through the Indira Gandhi Canal?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Canal carries water through Rajasthan and has transformed agriculture and settlement in parts of the Thar Desert.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental concern associated with the Indira Gandhi Canal?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies waterlogging and salinity, along with ecological-management issues, as concerns associated with canal irrigation in northwestern Rajasthan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which programme is identified in the PDF as an integrated initiative for conservation of the Ganga River?
questions.explanation: Namami Gange is an integrated programme for the Ganga basin that includes pollution abatement and other river-conservation activities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following activities is included under the Namami Gange programme as described in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists sewage infrastructure, pollution abatement, surface cleaning, biodiversity conservation, afforestation, and public participation among the activities of Namami Gange.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The National River Conservation Plan primarily supports which type of activity?

options.A: Pollution abatement in selected river stretches

questions.explanation: The PDF describes the National River Conservation Plan as supporting pollution-abatement activities in selected river stretches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a major factor influencing the climate of India?

options.C: Only the length of national highways
options.D: Only the distribution of mineral deposits

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies latitude as one of the factors influencing India's climate. Other factors include altitude, distance from the sea, relief, pressure and wind systems, and monsoon circulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical factor influences India's climate through differences in temperature with increasing elevation?
questions.explanation: Altitude is one of the climatic controls listed in the PDF. It influences temperature conditions across different elevations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the major atmospheric factors influencing India's climate?
questions.explanation: Pressure and wind systems are among the major climatic controls identified in the PDF, along with latitude, altitude, relief, monsoon circulation, and other atmospheric and oceanic influences.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only climatic factors listed in the PDF?

options.A: Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and relief
options.B: Mineral deposits, port density, and road length
options.C: Soil colour, population density, and industrial output
options.D: River islands, coastal harbours, and agricultural markets

questions.explanation: Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and relief are all listed as factors influencing India's climate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is India's climate described as a tropical monsoon climate?

options.A: Because of permanent westerly winds throughout the year
options.B: Because of seasonal reversal of prevailing winds and concentrated summer rainfall
options.C: Because the country receives rainfall only during winter
options.D: Because of the absence of seasonal changes

questions.explanation: India's climate is described as tropical monsoon because prevailing winds reverse seasonally and much of the annual rainfall is concentrated during the summer monsoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which monsoon supplies most of the annual rainfall to much of India?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon supplies most of the annual rainfall to much of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which monsoon is particularly important for the southeastern coast of India?
questions.explanation: The northeast monsoon is particularly important for rainfall along India's southeastern coast.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the PDF, which months constitute the cold weather or winter season in India?
questions.explanation: The cold weather or winter season in India is approximately from December to February.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which period is identified as the hot weather or pre-monsoon season in India?
questions.explanation: The hot weather or pre-monsoon season generally extends from March to May, with rising temperatures across much of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The southwest monsoon season in India generally occurs during which period?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon season generally lasts from June to September and constitutes the main rainy season in much of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which period is associated with the retreating or northeast monsoon season in India?
questions.explanation: The retreating or northeast monsoon season occurs mainly during October and November and may extend into December in some regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of India's winter season?

options.B: Cooler conditions and northeast trade winds

questions.explanation: The winter season is characterised by cooler conditions and northeast trade winds. Western disturbances also bring winter rainfall to northwestern India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The hot and dry local wind known as 'loo' is associated with which season?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies loo winds in northern India as a feature of the hot weather or pre-monsoon season from March to May.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kal Baisakhi thunderstorms are mentioned in the PDF as a feature of which season?
questions.explanation: Kal Baisakhi thunderstorms are associated with the hot weather or pre-monsoon season and are mentioned particularly in eastern India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which weather event is identified as a possible feature of the retreating monsoon season?
questions.explanation: The PDF notes that cyclones are possible during the retreating or northeast monsoon season.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The southwest monsoon reaches India through which two major branches?

options.A: Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch
options.B: Red Sea branch and Mediterranean branch
options.C: Pacific Ocean branch and Arctic branch
options.D: Indian Ocean western branch and Caspian Sea branch

questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon reaches India through the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain range receives heavy windward rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats and produces heavy rainfall on their windward side.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: After moving towards northeastern India, the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon generally proceeds westward along which geographical region?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal branch moves towards northeastern India and then westward along the Ganga Plain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an influence on the onset and progression of the southwest monsoon?

options.A: Seasonal low pressure over northwestern India
options.B: Permanent high pressure over the entire Indian mainland
options.D: Only the movement of ocean tides

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the seasonal low over northwestern India as one of the influences on monsoon onset and progression, along with land–sea thermal contrast, cross-equatorial flow, the Mascarene High, Somali jet, and upper-air circulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is specifically mentioned as an atmospheric influence on the southwest monsoon?
questions.explanation: The Somali jet is one of the atmospheric influences on the onset and progression of the southwest monsoon mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which high-pressure system is mentioned in the PDF as influencing the southwest monsoon circulation?
questions.explanation: The Mascarene High is mentioned among the factors influencing monsoon onset and progression, along with cross-equatorial flow, the Somali jet, and upper-air circulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are western disturbances?

options.B: Permanent tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal
options.C: Local summer winds originating in the Thar Desert
options.D: Southwest monsoon branches originating in the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: Western disturbances are eastward-moving extra-tropical weather systems originating around the Mediterranean–West Asian region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Western disturbances originate around which region?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Mediterranean–West Asian region as the source region of western disturbances.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which parts of India receive winter rainfall and snowfall due to western disturbances?

options.A: Northwestern India and the western Himalayas
options.C: Only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: Western disturbances bring winter rain to northwestern India and snowfall in the western Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Winter rainfall caused by western disturbances is beneficial to which agricultural crop season?
questions.explanation: Western disturbances can benefit rabi crops by bringing winter rainfall to northwestern India, although hail and other adverse weather may also cause crop damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a possible adverse agricultural impact of western disturbances?
questions.explanation: Although western disturbances can benefit rabi crops, they may sometimes bring hail and cause crop damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a rain-shadow region?

options.A: An area on the leeward side of a mountain range receiving less rainfall
options.B: An area that receives rainfall throughout the year
options.C: A coastal area receiving rainfall only during winter
options.D: A region where rainfall is caused only by cyclones

questions.explanation: Rain-shadow regions are located on the leeward side of mountain ranges and receive less rainfall than the windward side.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region is identified as a major rain-shadow area east of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau east of the Western Ghats is identified as a major rain-shadow region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the PDF, which two regions are also arid but for different climatic reasons?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies parts of Ladakh and western Rajasthan as arid regions, while noting that their aridity arises for different climatic reasons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: El Niño is generally associated with which tendency in Indian summer monsoon rainfall?
questions.explanation: El Niño is generally associated with a tendency towards weaker Indian summer monsoon rainfall, although it does not determine the monsoon by itself.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: La Niña is often associated with which tendency in Indian summer monsoon rainfall?
questions.explanation: La Niña often favours stronger Indian summer monsoon rainfall, but other climatic factors also influence the monsoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about El Niño and La Niña and the Indian monsoon is correct?

options.A: They alone determine the strength of every Indian monsoon
options.B: Neither determines the monsoon by itself
options.C: They have no relevance to monsoon variability
options.D: Both always produce identical rainfall conditions

questions.explanation: The PDF explains that El Niño and La Niña influence monsoon tendencies but neither determines the monsoon by itself. Several oceanic, atmospheric, and land-related factors also matter.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which oceanic phenomenon is specifically mentioned as influencing Indian monsoon variability besides ENSO?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean Dipole is specifically identified as another factor influencing Indian monsoon variability.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the additional factors influencing the Indian monsoon besides El Niño and La Niña?

options.B: Only the phases of the Moon

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Madden–Julian Oscillation, Indian Ocean Dipole, Eurasian snow, land conditions, and intraseasonal variability as additional influences on the Indian monsoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a major climate-related hazard in India?

options.C: Glacial calving in all coastal regions

questions.explanation: Heatwaves are among the major climate hazards listed in the PDF, along with cyclones, floods, droughts, cold waves, cloudbursts, landslides, lightning, and coastal storm surges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the major climate hazards affecting India?
questions.explanation: Cloudbursts are included in the PDF's list of major climate hazards in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following coastal hazards is specifically mentioned in the PDF?

options.D: Volcanic ash deposition across all ports

questions.explanation: Coastal storm surges are identified as major climate hazards, along with tropical cyclones and other extreme weather events.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the PDF, which factors shape exposure and vulnerability to climate hazards?

options.A: Settlement patterns, infrastructure, and land use

questions.explanation: The PDF explains that exposure and vulnerability to climate hazards are shaped by settlement patterns, infrastructure, and land use.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a classical factor of soil formation?
questions.explanation: Parent material is one of the classical soil-forming factors. The others are climate, organisms, relief or topography, and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains all five classical soil-forming factors?

options.A: Parent material, climate, organisms, relief, and time
options.B: Rainfall, population, transport, industry, and trade
options.C: Latitude, longitude, ports, minerals, and rivers
options.D: Temperature, roads, settlements, markets, and capital

questions.explanation: The five classical soil-forming factors are parent material, climate, organisms, relief or topography, and time. Human activity also modifies soil properties.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following soil horizons may be present in a typical soil profile?

options.A: O, A, E, B, C, and R
options.B: P, Q, S, T, U, and V
options.C: A, C, F, G, H, and J
options.D: L, M, N, P, Q, and Z

questions.explanation: The PDF states that a soil profile commonly contains O, A, E, B, C, and R horizons, although not all horizons occur in every soil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which soil type is widely distributed across the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra plains and river valleys?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soils are distributed across the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra plains and river valleys. They are formed from relatively young, stratified sediments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following crops is specifically listed among the major crops associated with alluvial soil?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists rice, wheat, sugarcane, jute, and pulses among the major crops associated with alluvial soil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a risk associated with alluvial soils?

options.C: Permanent water scarcity in all areas

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies flood and salinity risks among the issues associated with alluvial soils.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Black or regur soil is mainly associated with which geological formation?
questions.explanation: Black or regur soil is mainly associated with Deccan Trap basalt regions. It is clayey, moisture-retentive, and exhibits shrink-swell properties.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which physical property is characteristic of black or regur soil?

options.B: High sand content and very low moisture retention
options.C: High organic matter due to permanent waterlogging

questions.explanation: Black or regur soil is clayey and has shrink-swell properties. It also retains moisture, while drainage and cracking are important associated issues.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which crop is particularly associated with black or regur soil in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Cotton is one of the major crops associated with black or regur soil. Jowar and pulses are also listed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Red and yellow soils are mainly associated with which regions of India?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow soils are associated with Peninsular crystalline regions. The PDF notes their iron oxide content and generally low humus levels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which component is responsible for the characteristic colour association of red and yellow soils mentioned in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies iron oxides as a characteristic component of red and yellow soils. These soils generally have low humus content.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following crops is listed as suitable for red and yellow soils?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists millets, pulses, and groundnut among the crops associated with red and yellow soils.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Laterite soils are mainly associated with which environmental conditions?

options.C: Extremely low rainfall and no weathering

questions.explanation: Laterite soils are associated with high-rainfall and leaching zones, particularly in parts of the Ghats and plateaus.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following crop combinations is associated with laterite soils in suitable areas?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists tea, coffee, cashew, and rubber as crops grown in suitable laterite-soil areas. These soils are often acidic and nutrient-poor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic limitation of laterite soil?

options.A: It is often acidic and nutrient-poor
options.B: It is always rich in organic matter
options.C: It is permanently covered by snow

questions.explanation: Laterite soils are often acidic and nutrient-poor due to intense leaching in high-rainfall environments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Arid soils are mainly distributed in which part of India according to the PDF?

options.C: The wettest parts of the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Arid soils are associated with Rajasthan and other dry regions. They are generally sandy, low in organic matter, and sometimes saline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of arid soils?

options.A: Sandy texture and low organic matter
options.B: High organic matter in all locations
options.D: Formation only under dense evergreen forests

questions.explanation: The PDF describes arid soils as sandy and low in organic matter, with salinity occurring in some areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which soil-management issue is specifically associated with arid soils?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies wind erosion and salinity as issues associated with arid soils.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Forest and mountain soils are mainly associated with which geographical regions?
questions.explanation: Forest and mountain soils occur in Himalayan and highland regions. Their characteristics vary with altitude and vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which limitation is associated with forest and mountain soils on slopes?

options.A: They may be shallow and erosion-prone
options.B: They are always deep and free from erosion

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that forest and mountain soils may be shallow and erosion-prone on slopes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Peaty and marshy soils are mainly associated with which conditions?

options.B: Dry desert surfaces with little organic matter

questions.explanation: Peaty and marshy soils develop in waterlogged, organic-rich wetlands and lowlands. Changes to drainage can cause their degradation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of soil is associated with salt accumulation or sodicity in arid and semi-arid irrigated areas?
questions.explanation: Saline and alkaline soils occur in arid and semi-arid irrigated tracts where salt accumulation or sodicity can develop.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of management practices is identified for saline and alkaline soils?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies drainage, leaching, and soil amendments as measures required for managing saline and alkaline soils.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is soil erosion?

options.A: Removal and transport of topsoil by water, wind, or gravity
options.B: Addition of organic matter to soil

questions.explanation: Soil erosion is the removal and transport of topsoil by agents such as water, wind, or gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a cause of soil erosion mentioned in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies water, wind, and gravity as agents responsible for the removal and transport of topsoil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does soil degradation differ from soil erosion?

options.A: Soil degradation is broader and includes several forms of soil deterioration
options.B: Soil degradation refers only to the movement of sand by wind
options.C: Soil erosion includes every form of chemical pollution
options.D: Both terms refer only to the formation of topsoil

questions.explanation: Soil erosion specifically involves the removal and transport of topsoil. Soil degradation is broader and includes erosion, nutrient depletion, compaction, salinity, acidification, contamination, and loss of biological activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included under soil degradation but is not limited to the physical removal of topsoil?
questions.explanation: Nutrient depletion is one component of soil degradation. Soil degradation also includes compaction, salinity, acidification, contamination, and loss of biological activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agricultural practice is recommended for reducing soil erosion on sloping land?
questions.explanation: Contour ploughing is listed as a soil-conservation measure. It is used along the natural contours of land to reduce runoff and erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which soil-conservation method involves constructing step-like fields on slopes?
questions.explanation: Terracing is listed as a soil-conservation method in the PDF. It involves creating level or gently sloping steps on hillsides to reduce runoff and erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which soil-conservation practice involves growing different crops in alternate strips?
questions.explanation: Strip cropping is identified as a soil-conservation method. It helps reduce erosion by arranging crops in strips across agricultural land.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which structures are included among the soil-conservation measures listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Check dams and gully plugging are listed as soil-conservation measures that help control runoff and erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of shelterbelts in soil conservation?

options.A: To reduce wind speed and help limit wind erosion
options.B: To increase the removal of topsoil
options.D: To prevent all forms of rainfall

questions.explanation: Shelterbelts are included among the soil-conservation measures listed in the PDF. They help reduce wind exposure and limit wind erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following practices helps protect the soil surface by retaining plant residues or other protective material?
questions.explanation: Mulching is listed as a soil-conservation method. It protects the soil surface and helps reduce erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the biological and land-management measures for soil conservation?
questions.explanation: Controlled grazing is listed as a soil-conservation measure. The PDF also identifies afforestation, cover crops, and organic matter addition as useful practices.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which three dimensions of soil quality are maintained through soil health management?

options.A: Physical structure, chemical fertility, and biological activity

questions.explanation: The PDF describes soil health management as maintaining physical structure, chemical fertility, and biological activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which practice provides information about soil nutrient status and helps guide fertiliser application?
questions.explanation: Soil testing is identified as an important soil-health management practice. It supports balanced nutrient application and soil-test-based recommendations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of Soil Health Cards?

options.A: To provide farmers with soil-test-based nutrient recommendations
options.C: To record rainfall in every village

questions.explanation: The PDF states that Soil Health Cards provide farmers with nutrient recommendations based on soil-test results.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only soil-health management practices listed in the PDF?

options.A: Crop rotation, residue management, biofertilisers, and efficient irrigation
options.C: Uncontrolled burning, soil removal, and land degradation
options.D: Coastal reclamation, mining, and port construction

questions.explanation: The PDF lists crop rotation, residue management, biofertilisers, efficient irrigation, soil testing, balanced nutrients, and organic amendments as soil-health management practices.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of forest is characterised by very high rainfall, dense multi-layer vegetation, and no pronounced dry season?
questions.explanation: Tropical evergreen forests occur in areas of very high rainfall and have dense, multi-layer vegetation without a pronounced dry season.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following regions is identified as an area of tropical evergreen forests?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Western Ghats, Northeast India, and Andaman–Nicobar Islands as regions of tropical evergreen forests.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Semi-evergreen forests represent a transition between which two forest types?
questions.explanation: The PDF describes semi-evergreen forests as a transition between evergreen and deciduous forests.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a characteristic feature of moist deciduous forests?

options.A: Trees shed their leaves during a seasonal dry period
options.B: Trees remain permanently submerged in seawater
options.C: Vegetation grows only above the Himalayan tree line
options.D: Plants are exclusively adapted to extremely arid conditions

questions.explanation: Moist deciduous forests experience a seasonal dry period during which trees shed their leaves. The PDF lists teak and sal among their examples.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which regions are associated with moist deciduous forests in the PDF?

options.A: Eastern India, foothills, and wetter central India
options.C: Only the high Himalayas above the tree line
options.D: Only coral islands in the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies eastern India, foothills, and wetter parts of central India as regions of moist deciduous forests.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Dry deciduous forests are generally associated with which climatic condition?

options.A: Lower rainfall and a longer dry season
options.B: Very high rainfall without a dry season

questions.explanation: Dry deciduous forests occur in regions with lower rainfall and a longer dry season. The PDF associates them with the central and southern plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which vegetation type is characteristic of arid and semi-arid regions and contains xerophytic plants?
questions.explanation: Thorn and scrub vegetation occurs in arid and semi-arid areas and is characterised by xerophytic plants adapted to dry conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following regions is identified as an area of thorn and scrub vegetation?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Rajasthan, Gujarat, and rain-shadow interiors as regions associated with thorn and scrub vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of natural vegetation changes with altitude and includes temperate broadleaf forests, conifers, and alpine scrub?
questions.explanation: Montane vegetation changes with altitude and includes temperate broadleaf forests, coniferous forests, and alpine scrub.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which regions are identified as areas of montane vegetation in India?

options.B: Thar Desert and Rann of Kachchh
options.C: Eastern Coastal Plain and Coromandel Coast

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Himalayas and high Western Ghats as regions associated with montane vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Littoral, swamp, and mangrove vegetation are mainly associated with which type of environment?
questions.explanation: Littoral, swamp, and mangrove vegetation occurs in tidal and waterlogged coastal environments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following river delta regions is specifically associated with littoral, swamp, or mangrove vegetation in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists the Sundarbans and the Mahanadi, Godavari, and Krishna delta regions among the areas associated with littoral, swamp, or mangrove vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Alpine vegetation is generally found in which geographical zone?
questions.explanation: Alpine vegetation occurs above the tree line and is characterised by a short growing season. The PDF associates it with the high Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which climatic condition is characteristic of alpine vegetation?

options.B: Very high rainfall throughout the year

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies a short growing season as a characteristic of alpine vegetation, which occurs above the tree line in the high Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes tropical evergreen forests from deciduous forests?

options.A: Evergreen forests occur in high-rainfall areas with limited seasonal drought, while deciduous forests experience a marked dry season
options.B: Evergreen forests occur only in deserts, while deciduous forests occur only above the tree line
options.C: Evergreen forests shed all leaves simultaneously, while deciduous forests never shed leaves
options.D: Both forest types occur only in permanently waterlogged areas
