questions.explanation: The PDF explains that evergreen forests occur where rainfall is high and seasonal drought is limited. Deciduous forests experience a marked dry season and shed leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why do deciduous trees shed their leaves during the dry season?
questions.explanation: The PDF states that deciduous trees shed their leaves during the marked dry season to reduce water loss.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main basis for distinguishing moist deciduous forests from dry deciduous forests?

options.A: Rainfall and length of the dry season
options.C: Presence or absence of river deltas

questions.explanation: The PDF explains that moist and dry deciduous forests differ mainly in rainfall and the length of the dry season.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mangroves are best described as which type of plants?

options.A: Salt-tolerant woody plants found in intertidal tropical and subtropical coasts
options.B: Freshwater plants found only in mountain lakes
options.C: Desert plants found exclusively in sandy interiors
options.D: Alpine plants found above the Himalayan tree line

questions.explanation: Mangroves are salt-tolerant woody plants that grow in intertidal environments along tropical and subtropical coasts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important ecological function of mangrove forests?

options.D: Preventing the formation of river deltas

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies shoreline stabilisation as an important function of mangroves. They also store carbon and provide nursery habitats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mangrove forests provide nursery habitats that are important for which ecological function?

options.C: Increasing soil salinity in agricultural fields

questions.explanation: Mangroves provide nursery habitats and support coastal biodiversity. The PDF also identifies carbon storage and shoreline stabilisation as their functions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region is identified as the world's largest continuous mangrove forest region?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Sundarbans as the world's largest continuous mangrove forest region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is social forestry?

options.C: Conversion of forests into industrial areas
options.D: Removal of trees for expanding settlements

questions.explanation: Social forestry involves community-oriented tree planting and management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is afforestation?

options.A: Establishing forest on land that has not been recently forested
options.C: Converting forest land into agricultural land
options.D: Reducing the biological quality of forests

questions.explanation: The PDF defines afforestation as establishing forest on land that has not been recently forested.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is reforestation?

options.A: Restoring tree cover on previously forested land
options.B: Establishing forest only on land never previously forested
options.D: Removing all trees from a forest

questions.explanation: Reforestation means restoring tree cover on land that was previously forested.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which term refers to the conversion or removal of forest?
questions.explanation: Deforestation refers to the conversion or removal of forest. The PDF distinguishes it from forest degradation, which reduces forest quality and ecological function.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes deforestation from forest degradation?

options.A: Deforestation involves conversion or removal of forest, while degradation reduces forest quality and ecological function
options.B: Deforestation means planting trees, while degradation means restoring forests
options.C: Both terms refer only to natural forest growth
options.D: Forest degradation always means complete removal of every tree

questions.explanation: The PDF defines deforestation as conversion or removal of forest, whereas forest degradation reduces the quality and ecological function of forests.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is India considered a megadiverse country?

options.A: Because it has high ecosystem and species diversity
options.B: Because it contains only one type of natural ecosystem
options.C: Because all its regions have identical climatic conditions
options.D: Because biodiversity is restricted to its coastal regions

questions.explanation: India is considered megadiverse because it has high ecosystem and species diversity across the Himalayas, deserts, forests, grasslands, wetlands, coasts, and islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following ecosystems contributes to India's biodiversity as listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists grasslands among India's diverse ecosystems, along with the Himalayas, deserts, forests, wetlands, coasts, and islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How many global biodiversity hotspots are represented in whole or in part in India according to the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies four global biodiversity hotspots occurring in whole or in part in India: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as one of India's biodiversity hotspots?
questions.explanation: The Himalaya is one of the four global biodiversity hotspots identified in the PDF as occurring in whole or in part in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot is included in which group of hotspots identified in the PDF?

options.A: The four hotspots occurring in whole or in part in India
options.B: The biodiversity hotspots of Europe only
options.C: The biodiversity hotspots of South America only
options.D: The marine hotspots of the Arctic region

questions.explanation: Indo-Burma is one of the four global biodiversity hotspots identified in the PDF as occurring in whole or in part in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which biodiversity hotspot is listed in the PDF with the name Western Ghats–Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: Western Ghats–Sri Lanka is one of the four biodiversity hotspots listed in the PDF as occurring in whole or in part in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Sundaland biodiversity hotspot is represented in India through which island group?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Sundaland as a biodiversity hotspot represented in India through the Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an endemic species?

options.A: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic area
options.B: A species found naturally on every continent
options.C: A species that exists only in zoos
options.D: A species that migrates between all climatic zones

questions.explanation: The PDF defines endemic species as species that are naturally restricted to a particular geographic area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the term 'threatened species' under the IUCN categories?

options.A: It is an umbrella category covering Critically Endangered, Endangered, and Vulnerable
options.B: It refers only to species classified as Least Concern
options.C: It refers only to species found outside protected areas
options.D: It is identical to the term endemic species

questions.explanation: The PDF explains that threatened species is an umbrella category covering Critically Endangered, Endangered, and Vulnerable categories under the IUCN system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the term 'Endangered' is correct?

options.A: It is one specific IUCN category and is not synonymous with all threatened species
options.B: It includes every species in the Least Concern category
options.C: It refers to all species restricted to a particular geographic area
options.D: It is another name for the Near Threatened category

questions.explanation: The PDF distinguishes Endangered as one specific IUCN category from the broader term threatened species, which includes Critically Endangered, Endangered, and Vulnerable.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which IUCN category indicates an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild?
questions.explanation: Critically Endangered (CR) indicates an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which IUCN category indicates a very high risk of extinction in the wild?
questions.explanation: Endangered (EN) is defined in the PDF as indicating a very high risk of extinction in the wild.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which IUCN category indicates a high risk of extinction in the wild?
questions.explanation: Vulnerable (VU) indicates a high risk of extinction in the wild according to the IUCN category table in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the IUCN category Near Threatened indicate?

options.A: The species is close to qualifying for a threatened category
options.B: The species is already extinct in the wild
options.C: The species has an extremely high risk of extinction
options.D: The species has been evaluated and has the lowest possible risk

questions.explanation: Near Threatened (NT) refers to species that are close to qualifying for one of the threatened categories.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which IUCN category refers to species that have been evaluated and currently face a lower risk?
questions.explanation: Least Concern (LC) refers to species that have been evaluated and are currently considered to have a lower risk.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a biosphere reserve?

options.A: To conserve biodiversity while supporting sustainable development, research, and education
options.B: To promote mining as the main land use
options.C: To convert all natural habitats into agricultural land

questions.explanation: Biosphere reserves are large landscapes designated to conserve biodiversity while supporting sustainable development, research, and education.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which three zones are recognised within a biosphere reserve?
questions.explanation: The PDF states that biosphere reserves have core, buffer, and transition zones.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is listed in the PDF as an Indian biosphere reserve?
questions.explanation: Nilgiri is among the Indian biosphere reserves listed in the PDF, along with Nanda Devi, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Similipal, Pachmarhi, and others.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following biosphere reserves is associated with the Gulf of Mannar?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar is explicitly listed among India's biosphere reserves in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the list of Indian biosphere reserves given in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Achanakmar–Amarkantak is one of the biosphere reserves listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which island-based biosphere reserve is included in the PDF's list of Indian biosphere reserves?
questions.explanation: Great Nicobar is included in the list of Indian biosphere reserves provided in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is also listed as an Indian biosphere reserve in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Agasthyamalai is among the biosphere reserves listed in the PDF, along with Nilgiri, Nanda Devi, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Similipal, Pachmarhi, Achanakmar–Amarkantak, Great Nicobar, Khangchendzonga, and Panna.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Under which legislation are national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and conservation reserves recognised as protected-area categories?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides the legal framework for protected-area categories including national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and conservation reserves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which protected-area category generally provides the strictest protection among national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and conservation reserves?
questions.explanation: National parks generally have stricter protection. The legal regime and permitted activities differ among protected-area categories.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes wildlife sanctuaries in India?

options.A: All human activities are permanently prohibited in every sanctuary
options.B: They are exclusively established for commercial forestry
options.C: Specified rights and activities may be permitted under regulation

questions.explanation: Wildlife sanctuaries provide legal protection, but specified rights or activities may be permitted subject to regulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which protected-area categories are particularly associated with landscape connectivity and community participation?

options.A: National parks and tiger reserves only
options.C: Biosphere reserves and Ramsar sites only

questions.explanation: Conservation reserves and community reserves support landscape connectivity and community participation in conservation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Tiger reserves in India are notified under which legal framework?

options.A: Wildlife (Protection) Act and Project Tiger framework

questions.explanation: Tiger reserves are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act and the Project Tiger framework.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two broad areas are recognised within tiger reserves?
questions.explanation: Tiger reserves have core and buffer areas. The core area receives stronger conservation focus, while the buffer forms part of the wider reserve landscape.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Project Tiger was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to support tiger conservation through protected habitats and coordinated management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Project Elephant was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to support elephant conservation and the protection of their habitats and landscapes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes elephant reserves from national parks and wildlife sanctuaries?

options.A: Elephant reserves are always legally identical to national parks
options.B: Elephant reserves are landscape-level conservation units and do not necessarily have the same legal status as national parks or sanctuaries
options.C: Elephant reserves are established only in coastal regions
options.D: Elephant reserves are designated under the Ramsar Convention

questions.explanation: Elephant reserves are landscape-level conservation units under Project Elephant. They do not necessarily have the same legal status as national parks or wildlife sanctuaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is primarily concerned with the conservation and wise use of which natural resource?
questions.explanation: The Convention on Wetlands, commonly known as the Ramsar Convention, promotes the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Convention on Wetlands was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ramsar Convention takes its name from a city located in which country?
questions.explanation: The convention takes its name from Ramsar, a city in Iran, where it was adopted in 1971.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which year did India become a party to the Ramsar Convention?
questions.explanation: India joined the Ramsar Convention in 1982.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the primary international significance of a Ramsar Site?

options.A: It is a mineral exploration zone
options.B: It is a wetland designated as a Wetland of International Importance
options.C: It is an industrial development region
options.D: It is a national highway corridor

questions.explanation: Ramsar Sites are wetlands designated as Wetlands of International Importance under the Convention on Wetlands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Ramsar Convention?

options.A: Promoting the wise use of wetlands

questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention promotes the wise use of wetlands and international cooperation for their conservation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the supplied PDF, how many Ramsar Sites did India have as of 15 October 2026?
questions.explanation: The PDF states that India had 103 Ramsar Sites as of 15 October 2026, according to the Ramsar Secretariat. The total is dynamic and must be checked against the date specified in a question.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why should a question about the total number of Ramsar Sites in India include a reference date?

options.B: The number changes as wetlands are added to or removed from the list
options.C: The number changes only after every census
options.D: The number is determined by the number of states

questions.explanation: The Ramsar Site total is dynamic. The PDF specifically advises using the date in the question and verifying the latest official list.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which wildlife conservation programme was launched in 1973?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger, launched in 1973, is one of India's major species-conservation programmes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following conservation programmes is associated with elephants?
questions.explanation: Project Elephant, launched in 1992, is an important programme for elephant conservation in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is specifically mentioned as an important wildlife conservation initiative in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists crocodile conservation among important wildlife conservation programmes, along with tiger, elephant, rhino, snow leopard, vulture and sea turtle initiatives.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of species is included among the wildlife conservation initiatives listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Vulture conservation is one of the important species-focused initiatives mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a central tool of wildlife conservation?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies protected-area management, anti-poaching, habitat corridors and community participation as central wildlife conservation tools.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the conservation purpose of wildlife habitat corridors?

options.A: To connect habitats and support movement across landscapes
options.B: To convert forests into agricultural fields
options.C: To increase barriers between animal populations
options.D: To replace protected areas with industrial zones

questions.explanation: Habitat corridors support landscape connectivity and the movement of wildlife between habitat areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of agriculture practised in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists subsistence, commercial, intensive, extensive, plantation, shifting, dryland, irrigated, mixed, horticultural and organic farming as important agricultural types.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about agricultural types in India is correct?

options.A: Every farm follows only one agricultural type
options.B: Different agricultural types cannot exist in the same region
options.C: Actual farms often combine more than one type of agriculture
options.D: Only commercial agriculture is practised in India

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that although different types of agriculture are identified, actual farms often combine more than one type.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kharif crops are generally sown during which period?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon, generally during June–July, and harvested in autumn.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Rice is a major Kharif crop. Other examples listed in the PDF include maize, cotton, jute, soybean and tur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kharif crops are generally harvested in which season?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and generally harvested in autumn.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Rabi crops are generally sown during which period?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are generally sown after the monsoon, during October–December, and harvested in spring.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a Rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a major Rabi crop. Other examples listed in the PDF include barley, mustard, gram and peas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Zaid crops are generally grown during which period?
questions.explanation: Zaid crops are grown during the short summer period between the main Kharif and Rabi seasons.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a Zaid crop?
questions.explanation: Watermelon and cucumber are examples of Zaid crops mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major rice-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Assam among major rice-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is included among the major wheat-producing regions listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh is listed among the major wheat-producing regions, along with Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Bihar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is listed as major millet-producing regions?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh among the major millet-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major pulse-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh is listed among the major pulse-producing regions, along with Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major sugarcane-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Bihar among the major sugarcane-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major cotton-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat is listed among the major cotton-producing states, along with Maharashtra, Telangana, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is identified as major jute-producing regions?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies West Bengal, Bihar and Assam as major jute-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major coffee-producing states of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu as major coffee-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is identified as major tea-producing regions in India?

options.A: Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
options.C: Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Goa
options.D: Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Punjab and Haryana

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala as major tea-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which states are listed among the major rubber-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: Kerala and Tripura, along with other northeastern states, are identified as rubber-producing regions in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is listed among the major oilseed-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka among the major oilseed-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is identified as important spice-producing regions?

options.A: Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and Northeast India
options.B: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Himachal Pradesh only
options.C: Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh only
options.D: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha only

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and the Northeast as important spice-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched according to the agricultural production regions listed in the PDF?

options.A: Coffee — Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
options.D: Rubber — Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana

questions.explanation: Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are listed as major coffee-producing states. The other pairs do not match the PDF's regional list.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agricultural system involves clearing vegetation, cultivating land for a limited period and then shifting to another plot?
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation involves clearing vegetation, cultivating a plot for a limited period and leaving it fallow while cultivation moves to another plot.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is shifting cultivation commonly known as in Northeast India?
questions.explanation: Jhum is a regional name for shifting cultivation in Northeast India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The term 'podu' is associated with which agricultural practice?
questions.explanation: Podu is a regional name for shifting cultivation in parts of central and eastern India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which regional name for shifting cultivation is used in some parts of central India?
questions.explanation: Bewar is a regional name for shifting cultivation used in some central Indian areas. Jhum is associated with Northeast India, while podu is used in parts of central and eastern India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Green Revolution in India is primarily associated with increased production of which crops?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution refers to increased foodgrain production, especially wheat and rice, through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, fertilisers and improved agricultural practices.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The White Revolution in India is associated with which sector?
questions.explanation: The White Revolution transformed milk production in India through Operation Flood.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agricultural sector is associated with the Blue Revolution?
questions.explanation: The Blue Revolution concerns the development and expansion of fisheries and aquaculture.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Yellow Revolution is associated with increased production of which agricultural products?
questions.explanation: The Yellow Revolution is associated with increased oilseed production.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Operation Flood is closely associated with which revolution in India?
questions.explanation: Operation Flood transformed India's milk production and is associated with the White Revolution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of agricultural inputs and practices is associated with the Green Revolution?

options.A: High-yielding varieties, irrigation, fertilisers and improved practices
options.B: Only traditional seeds and rain-fed cultivation
options.C: Only plantation crops and organic manure
options.D: Reduction of irrigation and complete elimination of fertilisers

questions.explanation: The Green Revolution increased foodgrain production through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, fertilisers and improved agricultural practices.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which regions were the early gains of the Green Revolution concentrated?

options.A: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh

questions.explanation: The early gains of the Green Revolution were concentrated in irrigated regions of Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh before spreading to other states and crops.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an environmental concern associated with the Green Revolution?

options.B: Complete elimination of soil nutrient imbalance
options.D: Uniform agricultural development across all regions

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that the Green Revolution increased foodgrain output but also contributed to groundwater stress, soil nutrient imbalance, pesticide impacts and regional inequalities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which institution is abbreviated as ICAR?
questions.explanation: ICAR stands for the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, an important agricultural research organisation in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the full form of IARI?

options.D: Institute of Agricultural Revenue and Irrigation

questions.explanation: IARI stands for the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, which is listed among India's important agricultural research institutions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Central Rice Research Institute is now known by which name?

options.B: Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Central Rice Research Institute by its present name, ICAR–National Rice Research Institute.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which institution is specifically associated with research on wheat and barley?

options.A: Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research

questions.explanation: The Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research is listed among important agricultural research institutions in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which institution is associated with cotton research?

options.C: Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research

questions.explanation: The Central Institute for Cotton Research is identified in the PDF as an important agricultural research institution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which institution is associated with dairy research?

options.C: Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research

questions.explanation: The National Dairy Research Institute is listed among the important agricultural research institutions in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in agricultural marketing?

options.D: Only the export of agricultural machinery

questions.explanation: Agricultural marketing includes procurement, regulated markets, storage, grading, processing, cold chains, e-NAM and farmer-producer organisations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the full form of e-NAM in the context of agricultural marketing?
questions.explanation: e-NAM refers to the electronic National Agriculture Market, which is listed in the PDF as part of agricultural marketing.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which organisations are mentioned as part of agricultural marketing in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Farmer-producer organisations are included among the components of agricultural marketing, alongside procurement, storage, grading, processing, cold chains and e-NAM.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which scheme provides income support to eligible farmer families?
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN is listed in the PDF among important agricultural schemes. The PDF does not provide detailed eligibility or payment rules.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is associated with which area?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is listed among the important agricultural schemes in the PDF and is associated with crop insurance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which scheme is associated with improving irrigation and water-use efficiency in agriculture?
questions.explanation: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is listed among the important agricultural schemes in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which scheme provides soil-test-based nutrient recommendations to farmers through Soil Health Cards?
questions.explanation: The Soil Health Card Scheme is listed among important agricultural schemes. Soil Health Cards provide farmers with soil-test-based nutrient recommendations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which irrigation method involves diverting water from a river or reservoir through canals?
questions.explanation: Canal irrigation diverts water from rivers or reservoirs through a canal network to agricultural fields.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which irrigation method stores runoff in artificial or natural storage structures for later agricultural use?
questions.explanation: Tank irrigation stores runoff in tanks or reservoirs and makes the stored water available for irrigation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which irrigation methods obtain water by extracting groundwater?
questions.explanation: Well and tube-well irrigation extract groundwater for agricultural use.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which irrigation method delivers water close to the roots of plants?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water near plant roots, allowing water to be applied directly to the root zone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which irrigation method distributes water over crops in the form of droplets?
questions.explanation: Sprinkler irrigation distributes water as droplets over agricultural fields, resembling rainfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is lift irrigation?

options.A: Pumping water to higher command areas
options.B: Allowing groundwater to flow naturally without extraction
options.D: Distributing water through underground drip pipes only

questions.explanation: Lift irrigation uses pumps to raise water to higher command areas where gravity flow may not be possible.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region of India relies heavily on canal irrigation?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Gangetic plains and major river command areas are important regions for canal irrigation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is specifically listed among the regions using major canal irrigation systems?

options.C: Goa, Kerala and Arunachal Pradesh only

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh among the states using canal irrigation, along with Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Groundwater irrigation is particularly important in which of the following regions?

options.A: Northwestern plains and many hard-rock plateau regions

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies groundwater irrigation as particularly important in the northwestern plains and many hard-rock plateau regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main purpose of watershed development?

options.A: Integrating soil, water and vegetation management within a catchment
options.B: Increasing surface runoff and soil erosion
options.C: Replacing all groundwater sources with canals
options.D: Converting agricultural land into industrial areas

questions.explanation: Watershed development integrates soil, water and vegetation management within a catchment to reduce runoff and improve infiltration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is rainwater harvesting?

options.A: Capturing rooftop or surface runoff for storage or groundwater recharge
options.B: Diverting all river water into the sea

questions.explanation: Rainwater harvesting captures rooftop or surface runoff for storage or groundwater recharge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major objective of rainwater harvesting?
questions.explanation: Rainwater harvesting captures runoff for storage or groundwater recharge, helping conserve water resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a major water-management challenge in India?

options.C: Complete absence of urban water demand

questions.explanation: Groundwater over-extraction is one of India's major water-management challenges, along with uneven rainfall, river pollution, interstate disputes, floods, droughts and inefficient irrigation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which national policy provides broad principles for water planning, allocation, conservation and demand management in India?
questions.explanation: The National Water Policy provides broad principles for water planning, allocation, conservation, demand management and integrated river-basin management.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which National Water Policy is identified in the PDF as a key national reference?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the 2012 National Water Policy as a key national reference and advises checking the Ministry of Jal Shakti for updates and state implementation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main factor influencing the distribution of minerals in India?
questions.explanation: Mineral distribution in India reflects geological structure, including the nature of shield regions, sedimentary basins and coastal placer deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region of India contains many metallic and industrial minerals?
questions.explanation: Peninsular shield regions contain metallic minerals and many industrial minerals because of their geological formations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of resources is commonly associated with sedimentary basins in India?

options.A: Coal, petroleum, natural gas and limestone

questions.explanation: Sedimentary basins contain important resources such as coal, petroleum, natural gas and limestone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mineral is associated with coastal placer deposits in India?
questions.explanation: Coastal placer deposits contain minerals such as monazite, which is associated with thorium-bearing beach sands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is listed among the major iron ore-producing regions of India?

options.D: Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Jharkhand and Goa among the major iron ore-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major manganese-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Karnataka are listed among the major manganese-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major bauxite-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh among the major bauxite-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Malanjkhand, an important copper-producing area, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Malanjkhand in Madhya Pradesh is listed as an important copper-producing area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Khetri, an important copper-producing area, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Khetri in Rajasthan is listed among the important copper-producing areas of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Singhbhum is an important copper-producing region associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Singhbhum in Jharkhand is listed among the important copper-producing regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hutti, an important gold-producing area, is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Hutti in Karnataka is listed as an important gold-producing area. The PDF also mentions KGF as a historic gold-mining region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mineral is associated with the historic Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: KGF in Karnataka is identified in the PDF as a historic gold-producing region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major limestone-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Karnataka among the major limestone-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is listed among the major mica-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand are listed among the major mica-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is listed among the major coal-producing regions of India?

options.A: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal
options.D: Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Kerala

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana among the major coal-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major petroleum and natural gas regions of India?
questions.explanation: Assam is listed among the major petroleum and natural gas regions, along with Gujarat, Mumbai Offshore, Rajasthan and the Krishna–Godavari basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which offshore region is identified as an important petroleum and natural gas-producing area?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Offshore is listed among India's important petroleum and natural gas regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Barmer basin, an important petroleum region, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Barmer basin in Rajasthan is listed among India's important petroleum and natural gas regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Krishna–Godavari basin is important for which natural resources?
questions.explanation: The Krishna–Godavari basin is listed among the important petroleum and natural gas regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of energy resources is classified as conventional in the traditional classification given in the PDF?

options.A: Coal, petroleum, natural gas and large hydropower
options.B: Solar, wind, tidal and wave energy
options.D: Solar, biomass and geothermal energy only

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies coal, petroleum, natural gas and large hydropower as conventional energy sources in traditional classifications.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a non-conventional or newer renewable energy source in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is listed among non-conventional or newer renewable sources, along with wind, biomass, small hydro, geothermal, tidal and wave energy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the renewable energy sources listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is included among the non-conventional or newer renewable sources listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How is nuclear power classified in the energy-resource classification given in the PDF?

options.A: A separate low-carbon source using finite nuclear fuel
options.B: A renewable source like solar energy

questions.explanation: The PDF treats nuclear power as a separate low-carbon energy source that uses finite nuclear fuel, rather than grouping it with renewable sources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jharia, Bokaro and Giridih are important coalfields located in which state?
questions.explanation: Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih and North and South Karanpura are listed among the important coalfields of Jharkhand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Raniganj is an important coalfield located in which state?
questions.explanation: Raniganj is listed as an important coalfield in West Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Talcher and Ib Valley are important coalfields located in which state?
questions.explanation: Talcher and Ib Valley are listed among the important coalfields of Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Korba is an important coalfield located in which state?
questions.explanation: Korba is listed as an important coalfield in Chhattisgarh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Singrauli coalfield is associated with which pair of states?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Singrauli as a coalfield extending across the Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wardha Valley is listed as an important coalfield in which state?
questions.explanation: Wardha Valley is listed among the important coalfields of Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important petroleum and natural gas region associated with Assam?
questions.explanation: The Assam–Arakan region is identified as an important petroleum and natural gas region. Khetri, Singhbhum and Hutti are associated with mineral deposits listed elsewhere in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Tummalapalle, an important uranium occurrence, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Tummalapalle in Andhra Pradesh as an important uranium occurrence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Thorium is mainly associated with which type of deposits in India?

options.C: Iron ore deposits in plateau regions

questions.explanation: Thorium is associated mainly with monazite-bearing beach sands along parts of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is specifically mentioned as having thorium-bearing monazite beach sands?

options.A: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh
options.C: Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies parts of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as locations of monazite-bearing beach sands associated with thorium.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two states are especially identified as having high solar energy potential in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies arid and semi-arid regions, especially Rajasthan and Gujarat, as areas with high solar potential.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a key challenge in expanding solar and wind power in India?

options.A: Grid integration, storage, land, transmission and seasonal variability
options.B: Complete absence of renewable energy potential
options.C: Lack of any need for electricity transmission
options.D: Uniform energy generation throughout the year without variation

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies grid integration, storage, land availability, transmission infrastructure and seasonal variability as key issues affecting solar and wind energy development.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major factor influencing the location of industries?
questions.explanation: Industrial location is influenced by raw materials, power, water, labour, capital, markets, transport, ports, technology, land availability and environmental regulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains factors influencing industrial location?

options.A: Raw materials, power, labour, capital and markets
options.B: Rainfall, festivals, language and political parties only
options.C: Latitude, longitude and time zones only
options.D: Population age and sex ratio only

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies raw materials, power, water, labour, capital and markets among the important factors influencing industrial location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an agglomeration-related factor influencing industrial location?
questions.explanation: Agglomeration economies are specifically listed in the PDF among the factors influencing industrial location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of cities is associated with major iron and steel industry centres in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Jamshedpur, Bokaro, Rourkela and Bhilai among the major iron and steel industry centres, along with Durgapur, Burnpur, Visakhapatnam, Salem and Vijayanagar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which city is listed as a major cotton textile industry centre in India?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad is listed among the major cotton textile centres, along with Mumbai, Surat, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Indore and Kanpur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The major jute industrial belt of India is concentrated along which region?

options.A: Hooghly industrial belt in West Bengal

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Hooghly industrial belt in West Bengal as the major jute industry region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is listed among the major sugar industry regions of India?

options.C: Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Bihar among the major sugar industry regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major cement-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu among the major cement-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is listed among the major fertiliser industry regions?

options.A: Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Odisha
options.C: Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Tripura

questions.explanation: The PDF lists Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu among the major fertiliser industry regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which city is listed as a major automobile industry centre in India?
questions.explanation: Chennai is listed among the major automobile industry centres, along with Pune, the Mumbai region, Gurugram–Manesar, Bengaluru and Sanand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jamnagar is an important centre of which industry?
questions.explanation: Jamnagar in Gujarat is listed among the major petroleum refining centres of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is listed among the major aluminium-producing regions of India?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh among the major aluminium-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which city is identified as an important centre for IT and pharmaceutical industries?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is listed among the major IT and pharmaceutical centres, along with Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Mumbai, NCR and Ahmedabad.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched according to the industrial centres listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The Hooghly industrial belt in West Bengal is identified as a major jute industry region. The other locations are associated with different activities or mineral resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as one of India's major industrial regions?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Mumbai–Pune, Hugli, Bengaluru–Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Chota Nagpur, Delhi–NCR and Visakhapatnam–Guntur as major industrial regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are India's major industrial regions best described in the PDF?
questions.explanation: The PDF explains that major industrial regions are functional economic regions rather than rigid administrative units.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main purpose of an industrial corridor?

options.A: Integrating industrial nodes with transport, logistics, utilities and urban infrastructure

questions.explanation: Industrial corridors integrate industrial nodes with roads, railways, ports, logistics, utilities and urban infrastructure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which industrial corridor is listed as an example in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Delhi–Mumbai is one of the industrial corridor examples listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is another industrial corridor initiative mentioned in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Chennai–Bengaluru is listed among the industrial corridor initiatives, along with Delhi–Mumbai, Bengaluru–Mumbai, Amritsar–Kolkata and East Coast initiatives.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Bengaluru–Mumbai industrial corridor initiative is intended to integrate which broad type of infrastructure?

options.A: Industrial nodes with transport, logistics and supporting infrastructure

questions.explanation: Industrial corridors integrate industrial nodes with roads, railways, ports, logistics, utilities and urban infrastructure. Bengaluru–Mumbai is one of the examples listed in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an industrial corridor initiative in India?
questions.explanation: Amritsar–Kolkata is included among the industrial corridor initiatives mentioned in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: SEZ stands for which of the following?
questions.explanation: SEZ stands for Special Economic Zone. These are designated areas intended to promote exports, investment and employment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Special Economic Zones in India are governed by which legislation?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 as the legislation under which SEZs are designated.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major objective of Special Economic Zones?
questions.explanation: SEZs are intended to promote exports, investment and employment through specified regulatory and fiscal arrangements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about tax and incentive provisions in Special Economic Zones is consistent with the PDF?

options.A: Their provisions have changed, so outdated descriptions of tax holidays should not be relied upon
options.B: Their tax provisions have remained permanently unchanged
options.C: All SEZs are exempt from every form of regulation
options.D: SEZs have no regulatory or fiscal arrangements

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that SEZ tax and incentive provisions have changed and cautions against relying on outdated descriptions of tax holidays.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sectors has historically been developed by public-sector enterprises in India?
questions.explanation: Public-sector enterprises have historically played an important role in strategic sectors such as steel, petroleum, power, heavy engineering, defence, mining and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains strategic sectors historically developed by public-sector enterprises?

options.A: Petroleum, power, heavy engineering and defence
options.D: Only household services and local markets

questions.explanation: The PDF lists petroleum, power, heavy engineering, defence, mining, transport and steel among the strategic sectors historically developed by public-sector enterprises.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which factors have altered the ownership structures of some public-sector industries in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF explains that disinvestment, corporatisation and policy changes have altered ownership structures in some sectors.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major component of India's transport network?
questions.explanation: Roadways, railways, waterways, ports, aviation and pipelines form the major components of India's transport system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mode of transport is particularly important for providing last-mile access?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies roads as providing last-mile access within India's transport network.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mode of transport is important for moving bulk freight and passengers in India?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies railways as important for moving bulk freight and passengers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which transport infrastructure handles overseas trade?
questions.explanation: Ports handle overseas trade and are a major component of India's transport system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a potential advantage of inland waterways for freight transport?

options.A: They can offer lower-cost freight movement on suitable rivers and canals
options.B: They can operate only in deserts
options.C: They eliminate the need for all other transport modes
options.D: They are used exclusively for international air travel

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that inland waterways can offer lower-cost freight movement on suitable rivers and canals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which four metropolitan cities are connected by the Golden Quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata through a major national highway network.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main objective of the Golden Quadrilateral highway network?

options.D: Linking only major seaports with foreign countries

questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral improves road connectivity among the four major metropolitan cities of Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The North–South Corridor connects which two places?
questions.explanation: The North–South Corridor links Srinagar with Kanyakumari.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The East–West Corridor connects which two places?
questions.explanation: The East–West Corridor links Silchar in Assam with Porbandar in Gujarat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The North–South and East–West Corridors are major components of which programme?
questions.explanation: The PDF identifies the North–South and East–West Corridors as major components of the National Highways Development Project.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the organisational structure of Indian Railways?

options.A: It is divided into zones and divisions
options.B: It is divided only into districts
options.C: It has no regional administrative structure
options.D: It is divided exclusively according to state boundaries

questions.explanation: Indian Railways is organised into zones and divisions. The PDF also notes that zone boundaries and divisions may change.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as one of the major railway zones of Indian Railways?
questions.explanation: South Western Railway is among the major railway zones listed in the PDF.
